messages.body_plain:
Hi Simon,

I am currently working on an R package that calls Java through rJava and 
I would like to use intermediate callbacks from the Java side to R 
(again rJava, Rengine) before the Java side finished (backtesting 
framework that is written in Java, but uses R functionalities to compute 
asset allocations, main function that starts backtest in R).

My plan was also to use this package on an Rserve. Now, I saw this old 
thread 
http://mailman.rz.uni-augsburg.de/pipermail/stats-rosuda-devel/2011q3/001689.html 
<http://mailman.rz.uni-augsburg.de/pipermail/stats-rosuda-devel/2011q3/001689.html> 
where you strongly recommend to start the Java side first due to 
potential problems with system libraries (threaded vs non-threaded 
versions). Hence, Rserve which is pure non-Java would be non-reliable? 
Is there any OS where this approach is safe?

Thank you very much in advance.
Adrian
<http://mailman.rz.uni-augsburg.de/pipermail/stats-rosuda-devel/2011q3/001689.html>

Adrian,

On Jan 6, 2014, at 9:19 AM, Adrian Trapletti <adrian at trapletti.org> wrote:

> I am currently working on an R package that calls Java through rJava and I would like to use intermediate callbacks from the Java side to R (again rJava, Rengine) before the Java side finished (backtesting framework that is written in Java, but uses R functionalities to compute asset allocations, main function that starts backtest in R).
> 
> My plan was also to use this package on an Rserve. Now, I saw this old thread http://mailman.rz.uni-augsburg.de/pipermail/stats-rosuda-devel/2011q3/001689.html <http://mailman.rz.uni-augsburg.de/pipermail/stats-rosuda-devel/2011q3/001689.html> where you strongly recommend to start the Java side first due to potential problems with system libraries (threaded vs non-threaded versions). Hence, Rserve which is pure non-Java would be non-reliable? Is there any OS where this approach is safe?
> 

With Rserve you may be in a better shape. Main issues involve GUIs and their interaction with the main event loop, but with Rserve you don't have to worry about GUIs since there are none and Rserve fully controls the evaluation sequence, so you know whether you're re-entring or not. So the only thing to worry abut are a) no GUIs on the Java side (no AWT etc.) and b) synchronize re-entrance to R. Since Rserve doesn't use an event loop, I forget if REngine will synchronize for you or can only re-enter from an existing eval.

One more warning though - Rserve forks, so you have to make sure that you don't start Java before forking - most JVMs don't work when forked, so you have to connect first and then call .jinit(). 

Cheers,
Simon

messages.body_plain:
Here is one simple example. I assume you have no problem in installation
and you know little bit about R and Java.


import org.rosuda.JRI.REXP;  //Import whatever is required
import org.rosuda.JRI.Rengine; //without this we won't be able to make
'connection' with R consol


public class exampleR {
public static void main(String[] args){
String[] Rargs={"--vanilla"};   //check out
http://www.rosuda.org/r/nightly/javadoc/org/rosuda/JRI/Rengine.html#Rengine(java.lang.String[],
boolean, org.rosuda.JRI.RMainLoopCallbacks)
final Rengine re = new Rengine(Rargs, false, null); //the instance of
Rengine which will be used to apply R commands
if (!re.waitForR()) //precaution if we are not able to make connection
{
System.out.println("Cannot load R");
}
 REXP anREXParray= re.eval("runif(1)");   //creating an anREXParray of type
REXP and put a random no. in it. You can think of re.eval as a command
which pastes the "runif(1)" into R
//consol , calculates result and brings back result to java. Then it is
assigned to anREXParray.
double[] doubleARRAY=anREXParray.asDoubleArray(); //remember java doesn't
knoww REXP!! So, convert to know type for java
System.out.println(doubleARRAY[0]);
 }
}


suggestion: stackoverflow.com can be useful for future purpose.

Greg,

On Jan 30, 2014, at 9:07 PM, Gregory Dougherty <dougherty.gregory at mayo.edu> wrote:

> I have a simple and hopefully not too stupid question: What are the basic
> steps for launching and using REngine when you have rJava installed in R?
> 
> I've searched the web, and nowhere found a step by step guide on how to do
> this.  Is there one somewhere that I've just missed?
> 
> A set of instructions would be greatly appreciated.
> 
> Thank you,
> Greg
> 
> So far, I have
> (From the R side)
> install.packages("rJava")
> install.packages("Rserve")
> library(Rserve)
> 
>> From the Java side, this works:
> REngine eng = REngine.engineForClass("org.rosuda.REngine.JRI.JRIEngine");
> 
> But then calling this still fails:
> RConnection c = new RConnection();
> 
> Am I no longer supposed to use an RConnection?  Do we now just do everything
> with REngine?
> 

You're mixing two unrelated back-ends:

Rserve: client/server infrastructure for using R via TCP/IP or sockets from other systems
JRI: Java/R interface which allows you to load R into a JVM

org.rosuda.REngine is a backend-agnostic API that can interface either of the two above

org.rosuda.REngine.Rserve.RConnection is a subclass of REngine that use Rserve.
org.rosuda.REngine.JRI.JRIEngine is a subclass of REngine that use JRI

So my first question is - which of the two are you intending to use?

Cheers,
Simon
